The Patient Navigator Clinical 4 (PN4) utilizes specialized knowledge and skills to serve as a technical leader and recognized expert in clinical patient navigation within a defined specialty area. This position functions with a high degree of autonomy, coordinating highly specialized supportive care plans with goals and interventions based on treatment and individual patient and service provider needs. The primary responsibilities for this position consist of providing specialized clinical education regarding treatment; liaising with the patient's clinical service providers to address specific concerns; advocating for and representing the patient with a focus on satisfaction with the clinical aspects of their treatment experience; proactively identifying problems in clinical processes and operations and proposing solutions for situations with little or no precedent; developing and managing metrics to evaluate and improve program and patient outcomes; and taking a lead role in developing a culture oriented toward patient satisfaction.
90% - Nursing Process & Practice, Care Coordination and Patient Education

This position applies advanced specialized clinical knowledge within the field to assess patient needs, coordination of patient care, make appropriate referrals for specialized support services, and coordinate highly specialized clinical and non-clinical resources based upon patient diagnosis, insurance coverage, and community programs. The Patient Navigator Clinical 4 teaches, mentors, and coaches others in workflows and technologies as needed; creates and refines documentation and workflow standards; and proactively facilitates patient care coordination and communication. Independent judgment is exercised within the context of interdisciplinary and multidisciplinary approaches to patient care, and problem-solving frequently requires analysis of unique issues and situations without precedent or established structure.
5% - Clinical Education, Staff Mentoring & Patient Experience Culture
